topics.title: The First Miracle of Jesus
questions: What was the first miracle of Jesus?
Where did Jesus turn water into wine?

passages.note: Jesus turns water into wine at the wedding in Cana of Galilee. John calls it the beginning of His signs, and it manifested His glory.

topics.intro: At a wedding where the wine ran out, Jesus began His public signs.
applications: Bring your shortages to Jesus and obey His word even when His instructions seem ordinary.
Expect Jesus to provide more than the minimum.
illustrations: Idea: a host who discovers the pantry is empty minutes before the guests arrive.
discussion: Why do you think John calls this a 'sign'?
What 'empty jars' in our lives could we bring to Jesus?

topics.title: Faith
questions: What did Paul teach about faith?
What is faith?
Can faith move mountains?

passages.note: Faith even as small as a mustard seed can speak to a mountain and see it move; nothing is impossible to those who believe.
Faith is assurance of things hoped for and conviction of things not seen.
Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
Paul: the righteous shall live by faith.
Paul: justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul: a person is justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law.
Paul: saved by grace through faith - not from ourselves, it is the gift of God.
Faith without works is dead; real faith shows itself in action.
Jesus teaches believing prayer: have faith in God.

topics.intro: Faith is not a feeling; it is a confident reliance on God and His word.
applications: Take one concrete step this week that only makes sense if God is faithful.
Feed your faith daily by hearing and reading the Word.
illustrations: Idea: a person sits on a chair without testing it first - trust is shown by action.
discussion: What is the difference between faith and wishful thinking?
Where is God asking you to take a step of faith?

topics.title: Overcoming Fear
questions: How can I overcome fear?
What does the Bible say about fear?
Verses about courage

passages.note: God promises His presence, strength, help and upholding hand: fear not.
Be strong and courageous, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
God has not given a spirit of fear, but of power, love and a sound mind.
When I am afraid, I will trust in You.
Replace anxiety with prayer and thanksgiving, and God's peace will guard heart and mind.
Jesus gives a peace the world cannot give: let not your heart be troubled.

topics.intro: Fear is a common human experience; Scripture answers it with the presence of God.
applications: Name what you fear, then pray it through using Philippians 4:6-7.
Memorize one 'fear not' promise and repeat it when anxiety rises.
illustrations: Idea: a child walks through a dark house calmly while holding a parent's hand.
discussion: What does it mean that God commands 'fear not' so often?
How can the church help one another with anxiety?

topics.title: Faith During Trials
questions: How do I trust God during difficult times?
Verses about trusting God during difficult times
Why do Christians suffer?

passages.note: Jesus calms the storm: His presence in the boat is the answer to the disciples' fear.
Jesus promises trouble in the world but peace in Him - He has overcome the world.
Trials test faith and produce endurance, leading to maturity.
God works all things together for good to those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.
God has promised never to leave nor forsake His people.
God is refuge, strength and a very present help in trouble.
Present affliction is light and momentary compared with eternal glory; look at what is unseen.
God promises to be with His people through waters and fire.

topics.intro: Life often presents storms that challenge our faith - but we do not face them alone.
applications: Trust God even when circumstances seem uncertain.
Ask what God may be building in you through this season, and keep obeying while you wait.
illustrations: Idea: a ship's anchor does not stop the storm; it keeps the ship from drifting.
Idea: a refiner watches the furnace so the metal is purified, not destroyed.
discussion: Which promise helps you most in a hard season, and why?
How can we encourage someone who is suffering without offering shallow answers?

topics.title: Loving Our Enemies
questions: What does Jesus say about loving enemies?
Love your enemies

passages.note: Jesus commands love for enemies and prayer for persecutors, within the Sermon on the Mount.
Luke's parallel: do good to those who hate you, and be merciful as your Father is merciful.
Bless persecutors, do not repay evil for evil, and overcome evil with good.
Feed a hungry enemy: kindness can disarm hostility.

topics.intro: Jesus calls His followers to a love the world does not expect.
applications: Pray by name for someone who has wronged you.
Choose one practical act of kindness toward a difficult person this week.
illustrations: Idea: a ripple - one act of mercy changes the atmosphere of a room.
discussion: Why is loving enemies so hard, and what makes it possible?
Does loving an enemy mean allowing mistreatment?

topics.title: Jesus Feeds the Multitude
questions: Where did Jesus feed the five thousand?
Jesus feeding thousands

passages.note: Jesus feeds about five thousand men, besides women and children, from five loaves and two fish.
Mark's account: the disciples are tired, and Jesus has compassion on the crowd as sheep without a shepherd.
Luke's account: Jesus gives the bread to the disciples to distribute.
John's account: a boy's lunch is offered; the crowd calls Jesus the Prophet who is to come.
A second feeding: about four thousand men fed from seven loaves and a few fish.

topics.intro: Jesus meets real needs with what little we bring Him.
applications: Offer what you have - small gifts become much in Jesus' hands.
Notice the needs around you before sending people away.
illustrations: Idea: a boy hands over his lunch without knowing how it could possibly matter.
discussion: What does it mean that the disciples were asked to give the people something to eat?
What do you hold back because it seems too small?

topics.title: Peter Denies Jesus
questions: Who denied Jesus three times?
Did Peter deny Jesus?

passages.note: Peter denies knowing Jesus three times; the Lord turns and looks at him, and Peter weeps bitterly.
Matthew's account of Peter's three denials and the crowing of the rooster.
Mark's account of Peter's three denials.
John's account, with Peter warming himself at the fire.
Jesus restores Peter with three questions: 'Do you love me?'

topics.intro: Peter's failure shows how real weakness meets Christ's restoring grace.
applications: Do not trust your own strength; stay close to Jesus in the moments of pressure.
If you have failed, return to Him - restoration is possible.
illustrations: Idea: a bridge with a hidden crack - it looks strong until the load arrives.
discussion: What led Peter from boldness to denial?
How did Jesus restore Peter, and what does that say about us?

topics.title: The Lord's Prayer
keywords: our father which art in heaven
questions: Where did Jesus teach the Lord's Prayer?
How did Jesus teach us to pray?

passages.note: Jesus gives the prayer within the Sermon on the Mount, as a pattern for how to pray.
A disciple asks, 'Lord, teach us to pray,' and Jesus gives a shorter form.

topics.intro: Jesus did not just tell His disciples to pray - He showed them how.
applications: Use the prayer as an outline: honor God, seek His kingdom, ask for provision, forgiveness and protection.
Pray it slowly, a phrase at a time.
illustrations: Idea: a trellis - the prayer gives shape for your own words to grow along.
discussion: Which line of the prayer do you rush past?
Why is forgiveness tied to prayer?

topics.title: Prayer
questions: How should I pray?
What does the Bible say about prayer?

passages.note: Pray about everything with thanksgiving; God's peace guards heart and mind.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in everything - this is God's will in Christ Jesus for you.
Ask, seek, knock - the Father gives good gifts to those who ask.
Pray sincerely, not to be seen; the Father knows what you need.
The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective; confess to one another.
Jesus teaches that people ought always to pray and not lose heart.
Confidence in prayer: God hears us when we ask according to His will.

topics.intro: Prayer is conversation with the Father, not a performance.
applications: Set a short, fixed time to pray each day and keep it for a month.
Keep a prayer list and record answers.
illustrations: Idea: a child talks freely to a parent without needing perfect words.
discussion: What hinders your prayer life?
How do we pray when God seems silent?

topics.title: Forgiveness
questions: How do I forgive someone?
What does the Bible say about forgiveness?

passages.note: Be kind and forgiving to one another, as God in Christ forgave you.
Bear with one another and forgive as the Lord forgave you.
The parable of the unforgiving servant: those forgiven much must forgive others.
If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse us.
As far as east is from west, so far has God removed our transgressions.
Jesus on the cross: 'Father, forgive them.'

topics.intro: We forgive because we have been forgiven.
applications: Name one person you need to release and pray for them.
Confess any known sin to God today without making excuses.
illustrations: Idea: a cancelled debt - the ledger is torn up, not just postponed.
discussion: What does forgiveness not mean?
How is forgiving different from trusting again?

topics.title: Grace
questions: What is grace?
What does the Bible say about grace?

passages.note: Saved by grace through faith - a gift of God, not a result of works.
All have sinned, and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption in Christ Jesus.
'My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is made perfect in weakness.'
The grace of God has appeared, saving us and training us to live godly lives.
Sin shall not be master over you, for you are under grace.

topics.intro: Grace is God's undeserved favor shown in Christ.
applications: Stop trying to earn what has been given; serve out of gratitude.
Extend to others the grace you have received.
illustrations: Idea: a gift you could never afford, paid for before you arrive.
discussion: How does grace change motivation for obedience?
Where do you still try to earn God's approval?

topics.title: Hope
questions: Where can I find hope?
Verses about hope

passages.note: The God of hope fills believers with joy and peace so that they overflow with hope by the Spirit.
Hope is an anchor for the soul, firm and secure.
A living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
God's mercies are new every morning; great is His faithfulness.
God's plans for His people are plans for welfare and a future and a hope - spoken to exiles, so read in context.
'Why are you cast down, O my soul? Hope in God.'

topics.intro: Biblical hope is a confident expectation rooted in God's promises, not wishful thinking.
applications: Preach to your own soul as the psalmist does: 'Hope in God.'
Look for one way to encourage a discouraged person this week.
illustrations: Idea: a sunrise after a long night - the dark was never the last word.
discussion: How is biblical hope different from optimism?
What helps you hold on to hope in dark seasons?

topics.title: Salvation
questions: How can I be saved?
What must I do to be saved?

passages.note: God so loved the world that He gave His only Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have eternal life.
Confess Jesus as Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead.
Salvation is by grace through faith, not by works.
The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus.
Jesus: 'I am the way, the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Me.'
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.

topics.intro: The gospel is good news: what we could not do, God has done in Christ.
applications: Examine whether you are trusting Christ alone for salvation.
Share the gospel with one person this month.
illustrations: Idea: a lifeguard reaches a drowning swimmer - the swimmer must take the hand.
discussion: How would you explain the gospel in two minutes?
Why is the gospel good news and not good advice?

topics.title: Christian Leadership
questions: What does the Bible say about leadership?
How should a Christian leader serve?

passages.note: Jesus redefines greatness: whoever would be great must be servant; the Son of Man came to serve and give His life.
Jesus washes the disciples' feet and gives an example to follow.
Shepherd God's flock willingly, not for gain and not domineering, but being examples.
Qualifications for overseers center on character, family and reputation.
Jethro advises Moses to share the load by appointing capable leaders.
The apostles appoint Spirit-filled servants to meet a need so the word can keep spreading.
Where there is no guidance a people falls, but in an abundance of counselors there is safety.

topics.intro: Christian leadership is measured by service, not status.
applications: Ask the people you lead how you can serve them better.
Develop a successor: invest in someone who can lead after you.
illustrations: Idea: a shepherd walks ahead and behind the flock - guiding and guarding.
discussion: Where do we confuse leadership with control?
Who is God asking you to equip?

topics.title: Marriage
questions: What does the Bible say about marriage?

passages.note: A man leaves his parents, is joined to his wife, and they become one flesh.
Paul pictures marriage as a reflection of Christ and the church: mutual love and respect.
Two are better than one; a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
A description of patient, kind, enduring love.
Marriage is to be held in honor among all, and the marriage bed kept pure.
Jesus points back to creation: what God has joined together, let no one separate.

topics.intro: Marriage is a covenant designed by God, and a picture of Christ's love for His people.
applications: Schedule regular time to pray together and talk honestly.
Out-serve each other in small, daily ways.
illustrations: Idea: a threefold cord - strands woven so that the whole is stronger than any strand.
discussion: What does it mean to love sacrificially in marriage?
How can the church support marriages?

topics.title: Worship
questions: What is true worship?
What does the Bible say about worship?

passages.note: True worshipers worship the Father in spirit and truth.
Offer your bodies as a living sacrifice - this is your spiritual act of worship.
A call to sing, kneel and bow before the Lord our Maker.
Through Jesus, offer a continual sacrifice of praise to God.
Heaven's worship: You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power.

topics.intro: Worship is the whole-life response of creatures to their Creator and Redeemer.
applications: Prepare your heart before gathering with the church.
Bring thanksgiving into ordinary work this week.
illustrations: Idea: a violin in tune - everything in the life is brought into harmony with the Master.
discussion: What does 'in spirit and truth' guard us against?
How is worship more than singing?

topics.title: Evangelism
questions: How do I share my faith?
What is the Great Commission?

passages.note: The Great Commission: go, make disciples of all nations, baptize and teach, with Christ's presence promised.
The Spirit empowers witnesses from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
How will they hear without someone preaching, and how will anyone preach unless sent?
Be ready to give a gentle and respectful answer for the hope you have.
Believers are ambassadors of Christ, entrusted with the message of reconciliation.
Paul is not ashamed of the gospel - it is the power of God for salvation.

topics.intro: Every believer is sent: the message is Christ, the method is love and truth.
applications: Write down three people and pray for opportunities to speak with them.
Prepare a short personal testimony.
illustrations: Idea: one beggar telling another beggar where to find bread.
discussion: What keeps you from sharing your faith?
How can our church reach people in our community?

topics.title: Discipleship
questions: What does it mean to follow Jesus?
How do I disciple others?

passages.note: Jesus: deny yourself, take up your cross daily, and follow Me.
Abiding in Christ produces fruit; apart from Him we can do nothing.
Entrust what you have heard to faithful people who will teach others.
Jesus calls the first disciples: 'Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.'
Jesus calls His followers to count the cost.

topics.intro: A disciple is a learner who follows Jesus and helps others do the same.
applications: Find one person to walk alongside spiritually.
Choose a daily habit that keeps you abiding in Christ.
illustrations: Idea: an apprentice learns a trade by working next to the master, not only by reading.
discussion: What does 'take up your cross' look like today?
Who discipled you, and who are you discipling?

topics.title: Spiritual Growth
questions: How do I grow spiritually?
What is the fruit of the Spirit?

passages.note: Grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
The fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
Do not be conformed to this world but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
God who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion.
The one who delights in God's law is like a tree planted by streams of water.
Mature believers move from milk to solid food and train their senses to discern good and evil.

topics.intro: Growth is God's work in us and our daily response to Him.
applications: Build a simple rhythm: Word, prayer, fellowship, service.
Pick one fruit of the Spirit to ask God to grow in you this month.
illustrations: Idea: a tree planted by water - growth is slow, steady and unseen at first.
discussion: What spiritual habits help you most?
How do we measure growth without comparing ourselves to others?

topics.title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
questions: Does God provide for my needs?
What does the Bible say about God's care?

passages.note: The Lord as Shepherd: provision, rest, guidance, comfort in the valley, and a lifelong home with Him.
Do not be anxious: the Father who feeds the birds knows your needs; seek first His kingdom.
God will supply every need according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
The Lord who made heaven and earth watches over you and does not slumber.
Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.

topics.intro: The Shepherd knows His sheep by name and leads them through every season.
applications: Name the 'valley' you are in and read Psalm 23 aloud each morning this week.
Trust the Shepherd's guidance even when the path is hard.
illustrations: Idea: a shepherd with a rod and staff - guarding and guiding at once.
discussion: Which phrase of Psalm 23 is most meaningful to you now?
What does it mean that goodness and mercy 'follow' us?

topics.title: Love
questions: What does the Bible say about love?
What is love?

passages.note: Without love, gifts and sacrifices are empty; love is patient, kind and never fails.
A new commandment: love one another as Christ has loved you; the world will know His disciples by it.
Love is from God; God showed His love by sending His Son; if God so loved us, we ought to love one another.
God demonstrates His love for us in that while we were still sinners Christ died for us.
The greatest commandments: love God with all your heart, soul and mind, and your neighbor as yourself.

topics.intro: God defines love by what He has done in Christ.
applications: Look for a concrete way to meet a need for someone this week.
Measure your love by 1 Corinthians 13, not feelings.
illustrations: Idea: a parent sitting up all night with a sick child - love is shown in cost.
discussion: How is biblical love different from sentiment?
Who is hardest for you to love?

topics.title: Creation
keywords: created the heavens and the earth
questions: How did the world begin?
Who created the heavens and the earth?

passages.note: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
The Word was with God and was God; through Him all things were made.
The heavens declare the glory of God.
All things were created through Christ and for Him, and in Him all things hold together.

topics.intro: Scripture begins with God as Creator, and everything else follows from that.
applications: Receive creation as a gift and steward it.
Let creation lead you to worship.
illustrations: Idea: a painting points to the painter - creation points to its Maker.
discussion: What does it mean that humans are made in God's image?
How should creation shape our worship?
